title: 5 Best Smith.ai Alternatives in 2026
summary: Compare five Smith.ai alternatives for 2026, including per-call costs, usage fees, human coverage, and hospitality integrations.
body_markdown:
*Written by Punn Kam, ex-Google AI engineer and Y Combinator repeat founder. He is the co-founder of Conduit, an AI agent platform built for hospitality, serving 300+ hospitality brands in 140+ languages. Last updated September 16, 2026.*


Smith.ai charges by the call: 30 calls for $300, 90 for $810, or 300 for $2,100, with overage from $8.50 to $11.50 per call. For a hotel handling routine parking and check-in questions, those charges can add up. The comparison depends on your call volume and how much you value access to human receptionists.


## What is Smith.ai?


Smith.ai is a call answering and intake service. You can run it AI-first or human-first, and every plan includes live-staffed agents around the clock, described as professional call answering by real people trained in your field. That staffed coverage matters if you want a receptionist available when AI cannot handle the call.


Its named integrations are CRMs: HubSpot, Salesforce, and Clio. Clio is legal practice management, reflecting Smith.ai's focus on professional services. No property management system is named.


## What does Smith.ai cost?


Published plans, per month:


- Starter, 30 calls, $300, one free transfer destination, overage $11.50 per call
- Basic, 90 calls, $810, two free transfer destinations, overage $10.50 per call
- Pro, 300 calls, $2,100, ten free transfer destinations, overage $8.50 per call
- Enterprise, custom


Add-ons are metered separately: $1.50 per appointment booked, $0.50 per SMS notification, $0.25 for call recording, and $1.00 to accept a payment.


Calculate the cost using your own volume. Starter is $10 a call. As an illustration, a 200-unit operator taking 600 guest calls a month would pay roughly $4,650 on Pro pricing with overage, before appointment-booking and other add-ons.


## Why do people look for a Smith.ai alternative?


Call volume is one reason to compare alternatives. Per-call pricing can work for a business where a new client is valuable and calls are relatively infrequent. Hotels also receive routine questions about parking, access, and check-in, so include those calls in the cost estimate.


Access to reservations is another consideration. Smith.ai names HubSpot, Salesforce, and Clio integrations, but no PMS. Ask for a demonstration if you need the agent to read a reservation or change a checkout time.


## Which Smith.ai alternatives are worth comparing?


The table uses 600 calls a month as an example. Several vendors bill by minutes, credits, customers, or property units, so their final cost needs a separate calculation.

### Goodcall


Per agent from $79 a month, or $66 annually, with $0.50 per customer over the plan limit. Targets salons, local service businesses, and BPO. Cheaper than Smith.ai at volume, with no human fallback and Zapier-only integration.


### RingCentral AI Receptionist


$39 a month as an add-on with 100 minutes, or $49 standalone, with more minutes in bundles. Estimate the minutes you need before comparing the monthly cost.


### Quo, formerly OpenPhone


$19 to $47 per user per month with the Sona agent answering 24/7. It is built for small teams; confirm the AI allowance for your expected call volume.


### Dialpad


Dialpad uses conversation-based AI credits. Estimate usage to compare it with Smith.ai's per-call rates or a fixed seat price.


### Conduit


We build Conduit for hospitality. Pricing starts at $18 per unit per month, with a monthly credit allowance per unit. Calculate the cost using both portfolio size and expected usage. The same agent handles voice and text and can write changes back to the PMS. We report 70-90% automation across the platform. Conduit does not provide a human answering service: escalations go to your own team.


## Who should stay on Smith.ai?


Smith.ai is worth considering for law firms, agencies, clinics, and contractors with modest call volumes and valuable new-client inquiries. Its human receptionists and Clio integration are relevant to those workflows.


If staffed answering is a requirement, include that in the comparison. The other products listed here do not provide the same human answering service.


For hospitality options, see[best AI phone answering services for vacation rentals](https://www.conduit.ai/blog/best-ai-phone-answering-services-vacation-rentals) .


## FAQ


### How much does Smith.ai cost per call?


Roughly $10 a call on Starter (30 calls for $300), $9 on Basic (90 for $810), and $7 on Pro (300 for $2,100). Overage runs $11.50, $10.50, and $8.50 respectively.


### Does Smith.ai use humans or AI?


Both. You can choose AI-first or human-first, and all plans include live-staffed agents 24/7.


### Does Smith.ai integrate with property management systems?


None is published. Its named integrations are HubSpot, Salesforce, and Clio, which are CRM and legal practice management rather than hospitality systems.


### What is a cheaper alternative to Smith.ai for high call volume?


Compare RingCentral AI Receptionist at $39 or $49, Quo from $19 per user, and per-unit options for hospitality. Include minute bundles, AI credits, and other usage charges before deciding which is cheaper at your call volume.


### What additional fees does Smith.ai charge?


Add-ons cost $1.50 per appointment booked, $0.50 per SMS notification, $0.25 per call recording, and $1.00 to accept a payment, on top of the per-call rate.
